Not a checker-rule fixture: two node lines share the ID P1-N001 with
different titles (docs/backlog.md, "journal_tail's duplicate-ID
behaviour changed in the port"; routed here from node P1-N010's task
result). Run through the Python and TypeScript journal_tail
implementations directly (not through the checker), the two outputs
diverge in exactly the way that Backlog entry predicts:

- The Python implementation's ad hoc node-name lookup assigns into a
  dict in a line-order loop with no duplicate handling, so a later
  occurrence silently overwrites an earlier one — the *last*
  occurrence's title wins. Recorded verbatim in
  observed-python-journal_tail-output.txt.
- The TypeScript port's node-name lookup goes through the shared
  grammar unit (plan-register.ts), which reports a duplicate ID as a
  parse error and keeps only the *first* occurrence — so the *first*
  occurrence's title wins. Recorded verbatim in
  observed-ts-journal_tail-output.txt.

This fixture makes the divergence visible and does not resolve it:
deciding which behaviour is correct is a genuine tension between plan
decision 6 (preserve the Python's behaviour, record the deviation, fix
separately) and spec criterion D1 (journal_tail carries no grammar of
its own) that the Implementer of node P1-N010 flagged as arguably
needs-judgment rather than theirs to settle — and it still is not this
child's to settle. It is recorded here as evidence for whoever does.
